notes: THE RUNG PLATE (lane/rung, roadmap 21b). What the ward says about you the moment a Legend rung rises, in a docker's mouth and never the game's. One row per rung per track, keyed legend.<track>.<rung> (wire, roofs, flame, trade, law; rungs 1 to 4, legend.hpp's kLegendRungs), plus legend.top for the line a topped-out track gets under its own row. Each is ONE row on purpose: a rung is taken once a game, so there is nothing to rotate. Every row fits one line of the 4x6 font inside the plate at 320x180 (fifty-six glyphs and under), draws whole, and has no dash in it. The plate itself (native/src/render/rung_plate.cpp) prints the track's word and the new title from legend.cpp's own table over the row; NOTHING in the code writes a spoken line. Salted city-folk register, common words: the learned name for the priests' quarry stays in a priest's mouth and is not here.

rows: The rope hands know your face now. That is not nothing.
Coats get held shut when you walk by. They have heard.
Finch pours before you ask. That is a robber's welcome.
Nobody sees your hands. That is all the name means.
You went up and came down whole. The roofs noticed.
Slates do not creak under you now. Someone was counting.
The alley is a step to you now. The snug drinks to it.
Nobody looks up. You are what they'd see if they did.
You followed the trail. The Mission wrote you down.
The priests nod to you first now. The dockers saw it.
Doors open before you knock. Some folk cross the street.
You went down there and came back. Nobody asks you why.
Paid and on time. The counter remembers that first.
Your word buys on credit now. Not much. But some.
The Weighhouse stamps your paper without reading it.
Half this quay owes you. The other half is asking to.
The Watch has your name and is not sour about it. Yet.
Cull calls you by name across the room. On purpose.
Folk lower their voices when you pass now. Even sober.
When it goes bad, Vess says your name first.
There is no rung above that one. Mind how you wear it.
